name: Intuit

Software Engineer I (campus).dsaDepth: Moderate - an OA (MCQs + coding) then 2-4 technical rounds mixing DSA, CS fundamentals and debugging
rounds: Online round (HackerEarth): ~20 MCQs plus 2-3 coding questions, easy to difficult
Technical round 1: project discussion, C/C++/Java differences, OS/DBMS fundamentals, trees and graphs
Technical round 2 (some pipelines): a second, harder round revisiting resume projects and coding problems with multiple approaches discussed
HR/behavioral round: situational questions, company overview
extraTopics: Explaining language/paradigm trade-offs (C vs C++ vs Java)
Discussing multiple algorithmic approaches to the same problem, not just one solution

Software Engineer / Senior.dsaDepth: Moderate - a build-challenge take-home plus a tech screen focused on trade-offs and AI-tool usage, increasingly common in recent (2026) loops
rounds: Take-home "build challenge" (4-5 hrs, uploaded to GitHub)
Tech screen: questions on the build challenge, OOP concepts, and trade-offs made
Some 2026 reports mention explicit questions on AI-assistant usage in day-to-day development
extraTopics: Justifying trade-offs in a take-home project, not just completing it
Familiarity with AI coding assistants - recent interviews ask about this directly
Software Engineer / Senior.notes: Senior-level candidates report friction if leveling expectations aren’t aligned with the recruiter up front - clarify this early.
